name: Sunnyvale Home Access Grant
summary: Accessibility grants help eligible Sunnyvale households remove physical barriers with improvements such as grab bars, handrails, lifts, and ramps.
benefit: Home accessibility grant of up to $9,500.
eligibilityText: For lower-income Sunnyvale homeowners who are seniors or have a disability; current City income, property, and project rules apply.
sourceSnippet: The Home Improvement Program includes grants for accessibility improvements for lower-income households.

name: Sunnyvale Exterior Paint Assistance
summary: The Home Improvement Program can help eligible homeowners address deteriorated exterior paint through a self-help grant or contractor loan.
benefit: Up to $3,000 for self-help paint supplies or a loan of up to $6,000 for contractor painting.
eligibilityText: For lower-income Sunnyvale homeowners; City income, property condition, and project requirements apply.
sourceSnippet: The City's Home Improvement Program provides loans and limited grants for eligible home improvements.

name: Sunnyvale Roof Repair and Replacement Grant
summary: Limited Home Improvement Program funding may repair or replace a deteriorated roof that threatens household health, safety, or habitability.
benefit: Roof repair or replacement grant of up to $15,000, subject to funding.
eligibilityText: For lower-income Sunnyvale homeowners with a qualifying roof condition; limited funding and City review apply.
sourceSnippet: The Home Improvement Program supports health-and-safety repairs for lower-income homeowners.

name: Sunnyvale Emergency Home Repair Grant
summary: Emergency grants can address urgent health-and-safety repairs such as burst pipes, water heaters, heating systems, or sewer lines.
benefit: Emergency repair grant of up to $4,500.
eligibilityText: For lower-income Sunnyvale homeowners with an urgent qualifying repair; City review and available funding apply.
sourceSnippet: The Home Improvement Program offers limited grants for urgent health-and-safety home repairs.

name: Sunnyvale Energy-Efficiency Home Assistance
summary: City financing can support insulation, air sealing, weatherization, efficient appliances, heating systems, and window improvements.
benefit: Deferred loans up to $25,000 for houses or $15,000 for mobile homes, or a matching grant up to $5,000.
eligibilityText: For lower-income Sunnyvale homeowners; City income, property, and improvement requirements apply.
sourceSnippet: The Home Improvement Program includes loans and grants for qualifying energy-efficiency work.

name: Sunnyvale Housing Rehabilitation Loan
summary: Deferred rehabilitation loans can address plumbing, roofing, electrical, heating, windows, flooring, and wall repairs.
benefit: Loans up to $60,000 for houses or $30,000 for mobile homes.
eligibilityText: For lower-income Sunnyvale owner-occupants; current City underwriting, property, and project requirements apply.
sourceSnippet: The City provides rehabilitation financing for eligible lower-income homeowners.

name: Sunnyvale First-Time Home Buyer Loan
summary: The City offers down-payment assistance for eligible first-time buyers purchasing through Sunnyvale's Below Market Rate ownership program.
benefit: Second-mortgage assistance of up to $50,000.
eligibilityText: For moderate- or lower-income first-time buyers who live or work in Sunnyvale and meet BMR program requirements.
sourceSnippet: Sunnyvale's First-Time Home Buyer program offers a second-mortgage loan for qualifying BMR buyers.

name: Sunnyvale Library Homebound Delivery
summary: The library delivers selected books and other materials monthly to residents who cannot travel to the library because of a temporary or long-term disability.
benefit: Free monthly home delivery of up to eight library items.
eligibilityText: For Sunnyvale residents unable to visit the library because of disability; contact the library to enroll.
sourceSnippet: Homebound Delivery is available to Sunnyvale residents who cannot travel to the library due to disability.

name: Sunnyvale Youth Recreation Scholarship
summary: The 2026 Recreation Scholarship helps children join City classes, camps, and activities, with additional reduced-cost recreation benefits.
benefit: $500 per approved youth for eligible City recreation programs.
eligibilityText: For Sunnyvale residents age 17 or younger who meet income or qualifying-program requirements; funding is limited.
sourceSnippet: The 2026 program provides $500 per eligible Sunnyvale youth for City recreation activities.

name: Cupertino Youth Recreation Scholarship
summary: Cupertino partners with West Valley Community Services to help eligible local youth participate in City recreation programs.
benefit: Financial assistance toward qualifying Cupertino recreation activities.
eligibilityText: For Cupertino residents and Cupertino Unified School District youth; approval and available annual funds apply.
sourceSnippet: Youth recreation scholarships are administered with West Valley Community Services on a first-come basis while funds remain.

name: Cupertino Senior Center Membership Assistance
summary: Membership Assistance makes Cupertino Senior Center participation more affordable for eligible residents.
benefit: Scholarship covering up to 50% of the resident membership fee.
eligibilityText: For qualifying Cupertino Senior Center applicants; an application, documentation, and payment of the remaining fee are required.
sourceSnippet: The membership scholarship can cover up to half of the resident membership fee.

name: Cupertino Stay Active Fund
summary: The Stay Active Fund helps a Senior Center member participate in one class or event each year.
benefit: 50% of one class or event fee, up to $20 annually.
eligibilityText: For qualifying Cupertino Senior Center members; apply at the Senior Center and pay the remaining program fee.
sourceSnippet: The 50+ class and event scholarship covers half the fee up to the published annual cap.

name: Silicon Valley Hopper Discounted Fare
summary: SV Hopper provides app- or phone-booked shared rides around Cupertino and selected nearby destinations, with accessible vehicles available.
benefit: $1.75 discounted one-way fare instead of the regular $3.50 fare.
eligibilityText: Discounts are available to qualifying seniors, students, low-income riders, and riders with disabilities; documentation may be required.
sourceSnippet: SV Hopper offers reduced fares for seniors, students, low-income individuals, and riders with disabilities.

name: Cupertino CARE Resource Assistance
summary: Cupertino funds West Valley Community Services to connect lower-income residents with food, housing, emergency support, case management, and referrals.
benefit: Individualized resource navigation and possible basic-needs assistance.
eligibilityText: For lower-income Cupertino residents in need; West Valley Community Services determines service-specific eligibility and availability.
sourceSnippet: The City lists West Valley Community Services' CARE program as general assistance for low-income residents.

name: Cupertino Home Rehabilitation Assistance
summary: The City-supported Rebuilding Together program helps qualifying residents address home repair and rehabilitation needs.
benefit: No-cost or supported home rehabilitation services, depending on project and funding.
eligibilityText: For qualifying lower-income Cupertino households; property, income, project, and program-capacity rules apply.
sourceSnippet: Cupertino identifies Rebuilding Together Silicon Valley as a home rehabilitation provider for low-income residents.

name: Cupertino Adult Day Care and Caregiver Respite
summary: City-supported Live Oak Adult Day Services offers structured daytime support for older adults and respite for family caregivers.
benefit: Adult day services and caregiver respite support.
eligibilityText: For Cupertino residents who meet the provider's age, care, income, and program requirements; contact the provider for an assessment.
sourceSnippet: Cupertino lists Live Oak Adult Day Services for senior adult day care and caregiver respite.

name: Cupertino Senior Legal Assistance
summary: Senior Adults Legal Assistance provides free help with public benefits, housing, long-term care, consumer issues, elder abuse, and basic estate planning.
benefit: Free basic legal assistance for eligible older adults.
eligibilityText: For adults age 60 or older who live in Santa Clara County; appointments and service scope are limited.
sourceSnippet: The Cupertino Senior Center hosts appointments for free basic legal help through SALA.

name: Cupertino-Area Safe Parking Support
summary: The City identifies a rotating safe-car-park provider for people living in vehicles who need a safer overnight parking option and service connections.
benefit: Safe overnight parking and connection to support services, subject to availability.
eligibilityText: For people experiencing vehicle homelessness who meet the provider's intake and site requirements; space may be limited.
sourceSnippet: Cupertino's public-service page lists a rotating Safe Car Park program for unhoused assistance.

name: Cupertino Haven to Home Housing Support
summary: Cupertino funds West Valley Community Services' Haven to Home program to help residents experiencing or at risk of homelessness move toward stable housing.
benefit: Housing navigation and stabilization support; financial help may depend on need and available funds.
eligibilityText: For qualifying Cupertino-area residents facing housing instability or homelessness; provider assessment and funding availability apply.
sourceSnippet: The City lists West Valley Community Services' Haven to Home program under shelter and unhoused assistance.

name: Valley Water Landscape Rebate
summary: Valley Water rebates qualifying landscape conversion, irrigation upgrades, and rainwater-capture improvements for residential properties.
benefit: Up to $3,000 for standard residential projects, with higher caps in some cost-sharing areas.
eligibilityText: For qualifying Santa Clara County sites; application, pre-inspection, and approval are required before work begins, while funding remains.
sourceSnippet: Residential landscape rebates support lawn or pool conversion, efficient irrigation, and rainwater capture through June 30, 2027 or until funds are depleted.

name: Valley Water Graywater Rebate
summary: The program helps residents install qualifying laundry-to-landscape graywater systems that reuse clothes-washer water outdoors.
benefit: $200 or $400 rebate, depending on the property's water-service area and program rules.
eligibilityText: For qualifying Santa Clara County residential sites; obtain program approval before beginning work.
sourceSnippet: Valley Water offers a rebate for approved laundry-to-landscape graywater systems.

name: Valley Water Free Plumbing Fixture Replacement
summary: The Direct Retrofit Indoor Plumbing program replaces qualifying inefficient toilets, showerheads, faucet aerators, and related fixtures.
benefit: Free replacement of eligible inefficient indoor plumbing fixtures.
eligibilityText: For eligible Santa Clara County properties; income rules apply to individually owned homes and prior participation restrictions may apply.
sourceSnippet: DRIP provides free replacement of old, inefficient fixtures at qualifying Santa Clara County properties.

name: Valley Water Water Wise Outdoor Survey
summary: A free irrigation survey identifies outdoor water-saving opportunities and can help residents plan qualifying improvements.
benefit: Free irrigation-system assessment and water-saving recommendations.
eligibilityText: For qualifying irrigated properties in Santa Clara County; survey type depends on property and landscape size.
sourceSnippet: Valley Water offers free Water Wise Outdoor Surveys for eligible irrigated residential landscapes.

name: Silicon Valley Clean Energy Home Rebates
jurisdiction: Silicon Valley Clean Energy service area
summary: SVCE offers rebates for qualifying electric home upgrades such as heat-pump water heaters, heat-pump HVAC, cooking equipment, and electrical work.
benefit: Multiple equipment and electrical rebates, with additional income-qualified and selected city incentives where available.
eligibilityText: For qualifying SVCE residential customers and approved projects; equipment, installation, timing, and funding rules apply.
sourceSnippet: SVCE lists current home-electrification rebates and additional incentives for qualifying customers.

name: VTA Mobility Assistance Program
summary: VTA's Mobility Assistance Program distributes transportation resources through community partners to address access barriers.
benefit: Transit and paratransit fares or gas vouchers through participating community organizations.
eligibilityText: Intended for qualifying low-income residents, older adults, and people with disabilities in priority communities; partner agencies handle applications.
sourceSnippet: MAP provides transportation resources through community partners for residents facing mobility barriers.

name: RTC Discount Card for Riders with Disabilities
summary: The Regional Transit Connection card provides proof of disability eligibility and access to reduced fares on participating transit systems.
benefit: Reduced fares on VTA and other participating Bay Area transit services.
eligibilityText: For people with qualifying disabilities; application and documentation requirements apply.
sourceSnippet: The RTC Discount Card lets eligible people with disabilities pay Senior/Disabled fares.

name: VTA Senior, Disabled, and Medicare Fare
summary: VTA offers reduced bus and light-rail fares to seniors, qualifying riders with disabilities, and Medicare cardholders.
benefit: Reduced single-ride, day-pass, monthly, and annual fares.
eligibilityText: For riders age 65 or older, Medicare cardholders, or riders with accepted disability documentation.
sourceSnippet: VTA publishes discounted fares for seniors, riders with disabilities, and Medicare cardholders.

name: Clipper START Discount on VTA
summary: Clipper START gives eligible lower-income adults a discount on participating transit fares, including VTA bus and light rail.
benefit: 50% discount on eligible adult single-ride VTA eCash fares.
eligibilityText: Generally for Bay Area residents age 19–64 with household income at or below the program limit who do not have an RTC disability card.
sourceSnippet: VTA participates in Clipper START for eligible Bay Area adults with limited household income.

name: CalFresh Food Benefits
summary: CalFresh provides monthly food benefits through an electronic benefits card for qualifying households.
benefit: Monthly benefits to purchase eligible groceries.
eligibilityText: Eligibility depends on household circumstances, income, and program rules; Santa Clara County processes applications.
sourceLabel: County of Santa Clara Social Services Agency
sourceSnippet: The County application hub accepts CalFresh applications online, in person, by phone, mail, or fax.

name: Medi-Cal Health Coverage
summary: Medi-Cal provides free or low-cost health coverage to eligible California residents and families.
benefit: Comprehensive health coverage with costs based on eligibility.
eligibilityText: Eligibility depends on income, household, age, disability, pregnancy, and other program rules; the County processes local applications.
sourceLabel: County of Santa Clara Social Services Agency
sourceSnippet: The County public-benefits hub accepts applications for Medi-Cal health coverage.

name: CalWORKs Cash Assistance
summary: CalWORKs provides cash aid and employment-related services to eligible California families with children.
benefit: Monthly cash assistance and supportive services for eligible families.
eligibilityText: For families with children that meet income, property, residency, and other CalWORKs rules; the County determines eligibility.
sourceLabel: County of Santa Clara Social Services Agency
sourceSnippet: The County application hub accepts CalWORKs financial-assistance applications.

name: Santa Clara County General Assistance
summary: General Assistance provides county-funded cash support for qualifying adults without sufficient income or resources.
benefit: Time-limited or ongoing cash assistance depending on County eligibility rules.
eligibilityText: For qualifying Santa Clara County adults with very limited income and resources who meet County requirements.
sourceLabel: County of Santa Clara Social Services Agency
sourceSnippet: The County application hub includes General Assistance among available financial-assistance programs.

name: Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants
summary: CAPI provides state-funded monthly cash assistance to certain aged, blind, or disabled noncitizens who cannot receive SSI solely because of immigration status.
benefit: Monthly cash assistance generally aligned with SSI/SSP payment standards.
eligibilityText: For California residents age 65 or older, blind, or disabled who meet immigration, income, resource, and SSI-ineligibility requirements.
sourceSnippet: CAPI supports eligible aged, blind, or disabled noncitizens who are ineligible for SSI solely because of immigration status.

name: In-Home Supportive Services
summary: IHSS can pay for authorized in-home assistance so eligible older adults, blind residents, and people with disabilities can remain safely at home.
benefit: Authorized in-home help with personal care, domestic tasks, and related services.
eligibilityText: For qualifying California residents who are aged, blind, or disabled and meet Medi-Cal, functional-need, residence, and program requirements.
sourceLabel: County of Santa Clara Social Services Agency
sourceSnippet: The County explains how eligible residents can apply for In-Home Supportive Services.

name: Santa Clara County Senior Nutrition Meals
summary: The Senior Nutrition Program offers healthy meals and social connection at participating community sites in both Sunnyvale and Cupertino.
benefit: Community meals for older adults; voluntary contributions may be accepted.
eligibilityText: Meal-site participation rules vary; contact the selected site for age, reservation, schedule, and availability information.
sourceLabel: County of Santa Clara Social Services Agency
sourceSnippet: The County lists Senior Nutrition dine-in meal sites in Cupertino, Sunnyvale, and other local communities.

name: Transportation to Senior Nutrition Sites
summary: The Mobility Management Program helps qualifying Senior Nutrition participants travel to dine-in meal sites.
benefit: Possible monthly bus passes, gas cards, or paratransit rides.
eligibilityText: For low-income Santa Clara County Senior Nutrition participants who meet age, transportation-need, and service-specific requirements.
sourceLabel: County of Santa Clara Social Services Agency
sourceSnippet: The County offers free transportation resources to qualified Senior Nutrition participants.

name: California WIC
summary: WIC provides healthy-food benefits, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and referrals for growing families.
benefit: Monthly healthy-food benefits plus nutrition and breastfeeding services.
eligibilityText: For qualifying pregnant or recently pregnant people, infants, and children under 5 who live in California and meet income or linked-benefit rules.
sourceSnippet: California WIC offers food benefits, nutrition support, and referrals to qualifying families with young children.

name: California Alternate Rates for Energy
summary: CARE lowers electric and natural-gas bills for households that meet income or qualifying-program requirements.
benefit: Approximately 30–35% electric discount and 20% natural-gas discount for qualifying customers.
eligibilityText: For utility customers who meet current income limits or participate in an accepted public-assistance program; utility enrollment rules apply.
sourceSnippet: CPUC identifies CARE as an income-qualified electric and gas bill discount program.

name: Family Electric Rate Assistance
summary: FERA reduces electric bills for income-qualified households whose income may be above CARE limits.
benefit: 18% discount on qualifying electricity bills.
eligibilityText: For qualifying households served by a participating utility; current household-size, income, and utility requirements apply.
sourceSnippet: CPUC lists FERA as a lower electric-rate program for income-qualified households.

name: Energy Savings Assistance Program
summary: The Energy Savings Assistance Program provides qualifying households with no-cost weatherization and energy-efficiency services.
benefit: No-cost qualifying home energy upgrades and, in some cases, efficient appliances.
eligibilityText: For households that meet current CARE-linked income guidelines and participating utility requirements; available measures vary by home.
sourceSnippet: CPUC describes no-cost weatherization services for consumers who meet CARE income limits.

name: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program
summary: LIHEAP offers utility-payment help, crisis assistance, and weatherization services through local providers.
benefit: Possible one-time energy-bill assistance, crisis help, or free weatherization.
eligibilityText: For eligible low-income households; local providers prioritize applications based on funding, vulnerability, energy burden, and program rules.
sourceLabel: California Department of Community Services and Development
sourceSnippet: California LIHEAP provides energy-bill assistance and weatherization through local service providers, subject to funding.

name: Medical Baseline Utility Allowance
summary: Medical Baseline provides additional energy at the lowest residential rate for customers who rely on qualifying medical equipment or have certain medical needs.
benefit: Additional electricity or gas allowance billed at the lowest residential rate.
eligibilityText: For qualifying utility customers with a medical need certified under the participating utility's program rules.
sourceSnippet: CPUC lists Medical Baseline as an extra energy allowance for customers who rely on medical-related equipment.

name: California LifeLine
summary: California LifeLine provides discounted home phone, mobile phone, or eligible broadband service through participating providers.
benefit: One qualifying communications-service discount per household.
eligibilityText: For households that meet income guidelines or participate in an accepted public-benefit program; a participating provider starts enrollment.
sourceSnippet: California LifeLine explains enrollment through a participating provider using income or program-based eligibility.

name: Covered California Financial Help
summary: Covered California evaluates applicants for premium tax credits, cost-sharing reductions, state subsidies, or Medi-Cal through one application.
benefit: Possible lower monthly premiums and reduced out-of-pocket health-care costs.
eligibilityText: Financial help depends on household size, expected annual income, tax circumstances, residency, immigration status, and other marketplace rules.
sourceSnippet: Covered California offers premium and cost-sharing assistance based on household and income information.

name: CalABLE Disability Savings Account
summary: CalABLE offers tax-advantaged savings for disability-related expenses while protecting eligibility for many means-tested public benefits within program limits.
benefit: Tax-free qualified withdrawals and the ability to save beyond ordinary SSI resource limits under applicable rules.
eligibilityText: For people whose qualifying disability began before age 46 and who meet federal ABLE eligibility criteria.
sourceSnippet: CalABLE lets eligible people with disabilities save and invest for qualified expenses without automatically losing public benefits.

name: California Unemployment Insurance
summary: Unemployment Insurance provides temporary wage replacement to eligible workers who lose work or hours through no fault of their own.
benefit: Weekly unemployment payments based on earnings and eligibility.
eligibilityText: For workers who meet California earnings, work-loss, availability, job-search, certification, and other claim requirements.
sourceSnippet: EDD provides links to file and manage a California Unemployment Insurance claim.

name: California Disability Insurance
summary: Disability Insurance provides short-term wage replacement to eligible workers unable to work because of a non-work-related illness, injury, pregnancy, or childbirth.
benefit: Partial wage replacement for an eligible disability period, potentially up to 52 weeks.
eligibilityText: For qualifying workers with wage loss who paid into State Disability Insurance and meet medical-certification and claim requirements.
sourceSnippet: EDD administers Disability Insurance as part of California State Disability Insurance.

name: California Paid Family Leave
summary: Paid Family Leave provides short-term wage replacement when eligible workers care for a seriously ill family member, bond with a new child, or handle a qualifying military event.
benefit: Up to eight weeks of partial wage replacement in a 12-month period.
eligibilityText: For qualifying workers with wage loss who paid into State Disability Insurance and meet timing, work, care, bonding, or military-event requirements.
sourceSnippet: EDD states that Paid Family Leave may provide up to eight weeks of partial pay for qualifying family leave.

name: Supplemental Security Income
summary: SSI provides monthly payments to eligible people with limited income and resources who are disabled, blind, or age 65 or older.
benefit: Monthly federal cash payments, sometimes with a state supplement.
eligibilityText: For people who meet age or disability, income, resource, residence, and citizenship or qualifying-noncitizen rules.
sourceSnippet: SSA accepts SSI applications for eligible adults and children with limited income and resources.

name: Medicare Savings Programs
summary: Medicare Savings Programs are state-run programs that can help eligible people with limited income and resources pay Medicare Part A and Part B costs.
benefit: Help with Medicare Part A or Part B premiums and, depending on the program, deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments.
eligibilityText: Applicants generally must have Medicare and meet the income, resource, and other rules for one of four programs: QMB, SLMB, QI, or QDWI. California makes the final eligibility decision, and limits may change each year.
sourceSnippet: Medicare explains the four Medicare Savings Programs, the costs each may cover, current qualification guidance, and how to contact the state to apply.

name: Medicare Part D Extra Help
summary: Extra Help lowers Medicare Part D prescription-drug costs for eligible people with limited income and resources.
benefit: Help paying Medicare drug-plan premiums, deductibles, coinsurance, copayments, and other Part D costs; the Part D late-enrollment penalty is waived while receiving Extra Help.
eligibilityText: Eligibility generally requires Medicare and meeting current income and resource rules. People receiving full Medicaid, help with Part B premiums through a Medicare Savings Program, or SSI may qualify automatically; others can apply through Social Security.
sourceSnippet: Medicare and Social Security explain who receives Extra Help automatically, who should apply, the costs it may reduce, and the online application process.

name: Social Security Disability Insurance
summary: SSDI pays monthly benefits to eligible workers whose qualifying disability prevents substantial work and who have sufficient Social Security work history.
benefit: Monthly disability payments based on the worker's earnings record.
eligibilityText: For people who meet Social Security's disability standard and insured-work-credit requirements; waiting periods and other rules may apply.
sourceSnippet: SSA explains online and phone application paths for Social Security disability benefits.

name: VA Disability Compensation
summary: VA disability compensation provides tax-free monthly payments for qualifying illnesses or injuries caused or worsened by active military service.
benefit: Tax-free monthly compensation based on the VA disability rating and eligible dependents.
eligibilityText: For eligible Veterans or service members with a service-connected condition and qualifying discharge or service history; evidence is required.
sourceSnippet: VA provides online, mail, in-person, fax, and accredited-representative paths for disability claims.

name: VA Health Care
summary: VA health care offers eligible Veterans preventive, primary, specialty, mental-health, and other covered services.
benefit: VA health coverage and access to covered care, with copays based on eligibility and priority group.
eligibilityText: Generally for eligible Veterans with qualifying active-duty service and discharge status; service history, disability, income, and other factors may affect enrollment.
sourceSnippet: VA explains health-care benefits and application options for potentially eligible Veterans.

name: VA Veterans Pension
summary: VA pension provides monthly payments to some wartime Veterans with limited income and net worth who meet age or disability rules.
benefit: Monthly pension payment based on income, net worth, dependents, and additional care needs.
eligibilityText: For qualifying wartime Veterans with acceptable discharge, required service, income and net-worth limits, plus age 65 or qualifying disability or care status.
sourceSnippet: VA Pension supports qualifying wartime Veterans who meet service, financial, age, or disability requirements.

name: Federal Child Tax Credit
summary: The Child Tax Credit can reduce federal income tax for families with a qualifying child, and some families may receive a refundable Additional Child Tax Credit.
benefit: A federal tax credit for each qualifying child; the amount and refundable portion depend on the tax year and household circumstances.
eligibilityText: Eligibility generally depends on the child's age, relationship, residency, dependent status, Social Security number, and the taxpayer's income and filing circumstances.
sourceSnippet: The IRS explains the Child Tax Credit, refundable Additional Child Tax Credit, qualifying-child rules, and how to claim the credit on a federal return.

name: Federal Child and Dependent Care Credit
summary: This federal credit may offset part of the cost of care that allows a taxpayer to work or look for work, including eligible child care and care for a spouse or dependent who cannot care for themselves.
benefit: A federal tax credit based on a percentage of eligible work-related care expenses, subject to annual limits and tax-year rules.
eligibilityText: Generally requires earned income and qualifying work-related care expenses for a child under 13 or a spouse or dependent who cannot care for themselves; filing-status and care-provider rules apply.
sourceSnippet: IRS Publication 503 explains qualifying people, eligible care expenses, earned-income rules, expense limits, and Form 2441.

name: Federal Earned Income Tax Credit
summary: The Earned Income Tax Credit is a refundable federal credit for eligible workers and families with low to moderate earned income, with or without qualifying children.
benefit: A refundable federal tax credit whose amount varies by earned income, filing status, and number of qualifying children.
eligibilityText: Requires qualifying earned income and compliance with income, investment-income, filing-status, residency, identification-number, and qualifying-child rules that apply to the tax year.
sourceSnippet: The IRS provides current EITC rules, income limits, an eligibility assistant, and instructions for claiming the credit on a federal return.

name: California Child and Dependent Care Expenses Credit
summary: California may provide a state income-tax credit when a taxpayer pays for qualifying child or dependent care in California so they can work or look for work.
benefit: A nonrefundable California tax credit based on a percentage of eligible care expenses, subject to income and expense limits.
eligibilityText: Generally requires earned income, federal adjusted gross income of $100,000 or less, California-provided care, and qualifying work-related care for a child under 13 or another qualifying person.
sourceSnippet: The Franchise Tax Board explains eligibility, eligible expense limits, and how to claim the credit using FTB Form 3506.

name: California Earned Income Tax Credit
summary: CalEITC is a refundable California tax credit for eligible low-income workers and families, including people who do not have a qualifying child.
benefit: Up to $3,756 for tax year 2025, depending on earned income and qualifying children; filing or amending a California return is required.
eligibilityText: For eligible California workers and families with 2025 earned income and federal adjusted gross income below $32,901; age, residency, identification-number, filing, and dependent rules apply.
sourceSnippet: The Franchise Tax Board states that eligible working Californians may claim CalEITC by filing a state return and FTB Form 3514.

name: California Young Child Tax Credit
summary: The Young Child Tax Credit is a refundable California credit for eligible households with a qualifying child younger than six.
benefit: Up to $1,189 per eligible tax return for tax year 2025, which may provide cash back or reduce state tax owed.
eligibilityText: Generally requires a qualifying child under age six and meeting CalEITC-related income, residency, filing, and identification-number rules; special rules allow some households with no earned income or a net loss.
sourceSnippet: The Franchise Tax Board explains the refundable Young Child Tax Credit and how to claim it with FTB Form 3514.

name: California Subsidized Child Care
summary: California supports voucher-based and center-based child-care programs that can help eligible families pay for care through CalWORKs and other subsidized child-care pathways.
benefit: Full or partial payment of eligible child-care costs through a voucher or a subsidized child-care provider, depending on the program and available space.
eligibilityText: Programs use income or categorical eligibility plus a qualifying need for care, such as employment, education, training, seeking permanent housing, or child-protective circumstances; program availability and family fees vary.
sourceSnippet: CDSS describes California's voucher-based and direct-service subsidized child-care programs and directs families to local resource-and-referral and alternative-payment agencies.
